0.long_answer: Oculofaciocardiodental syndrome is the subtype of syndromic microphthalmia that is associated with mutations in the BCOR gene. This condition, often referred to as the X-linked BCOR microphthalmia syndrome, involves a constellation of ocular, facial, cardiac, and dental anomalies. Multiple studies have documented novel mutations in the BCOR gene in patients displaying the clinical features of this syndrome, solidifying its association with this particular genetic alteration. While other microphthalmia syndromes exist, the evidence specifically links BCOR mutations to the development of oculofaciocardiodental syndrome rather than to other types like Lenz microphthalmia syndrome.
